subject: Spanska
title: Adjectives and descriptions
sourceSummary: How adjectives agree in gender and number, and where adjectives are placed in a sentence.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Mi hermano es ___." (alto = tall)
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in -o agree with the noun: masculine singular "hermano" → "alto".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Mis hermanas son ___." (simpático = nice)
questions.explanation: Feminine plural is formed with -as: "simpáticas". The adjective must agree with "hermanas" in both gender and number.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "El libro es ___." (interesante = interesting)
questions.opener: Adjectives ending in -e don't change with gender.
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in -e, like "interesante", have the same form for masculine and feminine — only the plural changes ("interesantes").

questions.prompt: Where are most descriptive adjectives placed in Spanish?
questions.opener: This differs from Swedish, where the adjective usually comes before the noun.
questions.explanation: Most descriptive adjectives come after the noun: "una casa grande" (a big house), not "una grande casa". However, some common adjectives (like bueno/malo) can go before the noun.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence for "the black cats":
questions.explanation: "Gatos" is masculine plural, so the adjective must be too: "negros". The article "los" (masculine plural) already agrees.

questions.prompt: Write the feminine singular form of "pequeño" (small).
Correct the error: "Mis amigas son muy divertido." (My friends (girls) are very fun.)
questions.opener: Check the gender and number of "amigas".
steps: "Amigas" is feminine plural, so the adjective "divertido" (which is masculine singular) must change.
The full sentence: "Mis amigas son muy divertidas." (My friends are very fun.)

questions.prompt: How do Spanish adjectives agree in gender and number, and where are they placed?
questions.opener: Adjectives "agree" with the noun they describe.
questions.answer: Adjectives ending in -o: alto/alta/altos/altas (agree in gender and number). Adjectives ending in -e: interesante/interesantes (same form for both genders, only the plural changes). Adjectives ending in a consonant: joven/jóvenes (plural with -es). Placement: most descriptive adjectives come AFTER the noun (una casa grande), unlike in Swedish. Examples: gato negro (black cat), casa pequeña (small house), chicas simpáticas (nice girls).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Los coches son ___." (rápido = fast)
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in -o agree with the noun: masculine plural "coches" → "rápidos".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "La chica es ___." (inteligente = intelligent)
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in -e have the same form regardless of gender: "la chica es inteligente" and "el chico es inteligente" both use "inteligente".

questions.prompt: Which adjective is often placed BEFORE the noun in Spanish, unlike most others?
questions.opener: This adjective is often shortened to "buen" and can be placed before the noun, e.g. "un buen amigo".
questions.explanation: "Bueno" (in the shortened form "buen") is one of the common adjectives often placed BEFORE the noun in Spanish, unlike most descriptive adjectives, which come after.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural form of "joven" (young): "Mis primos son ___."
questions.opener: "Joven" ends in a consonant, just like "profesor".
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in a consonant form the plural with -es: "joven" → "jóvenes" (note the accent shift to keep the pronunciation).

questions.prompt: What does the sentence "Es un chico muy trabajador" mean?
questions.opener: The word "trabajador" is related to the verb trabajar (to work).
choices: He is a very hard-working guy
He is a very lazy guy
He is a very funny guy
He is a very young guy
questions.explanation: "Es un chico muy trabajador" means "he is a very hard-working guy".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Estas manzanas están ___." (verde = green, unripe)
questions.explanation: "Verde" has the same form regardless of gender, but becomes plural "verdes" with "manzanas" (apples, plural).

questions.prompt: Which word pair describes opposites in Spanish: "grande" and...?
questions.explanation: "Pequeño" means "small" and is the opposite of "grande" (big).
